exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.icc_size_origin: JpegDecoderHelper::getICCSize() = mICCBuffer.size(); mICCBuffer is a std::vector<JOCTET> filled by jpeg_extract_marker_payload() from a JPEG APP2 marker whose payload begins with 'ICC_PROFILE\0' (12-byte sig); destination.resize(marker->data_length) — one APP2 marker only (first match wins, returns immediately).
exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.marker_data_length_bound: libjpeg (libjpeg-turbo, bundled mozjpeg in sharp-libvips) enforces a 16-bit marker length field: data_length = 2-byte unsigned big-endian length minus 2, so data_length <= 65533. Additionally jpeg_save_markers(kAPP2Marker, 0xFFFF) preserves up to 65535 bytes of payload, and libjpeg's jpeg_read_marker limits marker length to 65533 bytes.
exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.provenance_chain: HTTP request body (image bytes) -> Next.js image-optimizer -> sharp(jpeg) decode -> libvips jpeg loader (libjpeg marker list) -> ultrahdr decode path (jpegr.cpp:338/1493/1521 jpeg_dec_obj.getICCSize()) -> readIccColorGamut(icc_data, icc_size)
exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.attacker_control: YES in principle: the ICC APP2 payload bytes are attacker-controlled image content. The alignment branch (unaligned pointer) makes the new[] reachability data-dependent, but the SIZE passed is exactly icc_size - 14.
exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.conversions: icc_size - kICCIdentifierSize: size_t arithmetic; guarded by the early return icc_size >= 132+14 (icc.cpp:644), so no underflow. align_val_t value = 4 (alignof(ICCHeader)). The gcc-12 aligned_alloc rounding wraps iff sz + 4 - 1 >= 2^64, i.e. sz >= 2^64 - 3 — impossible for sz <= 65533.
exact_type_and_semantics_of_size.hard_upper_bound: 65533 - 14 = 65519 bytes (ICC APP2 payload capped by the 16-bit JPEG marker length field), OR by libvips/sharp input size limits — either way << 2^64 - 3.

mathematical_conclusion.conclusion: The libvips/libuhdr aligned-new call CANNOT reach the CVE-2026-95619 overflow: the size is hard-bounded by the JPEG marker 16-bit length field to <= 65519 bytes, at least 2^48 below the exact threshold. Attacker can control the size value only within that bound; wraparound is arithmetically impossible.
